title: Massapeoque Meadows / South Oyster Bay
summary: Massapeoque and Massapequa records preserve references to meadow landscapes and south shore salt meadows. These records point to wetlands as named, used, and negotiated places, not marginal land. The South Oyster Bay meadow landscape was part of hunting, fishing, shellfishing, travel, and later colonial claims over land and resources.
address_label: South Oyster Bay marsh and meadow landscape, Massapequa-Seaford area
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land with note that Massapequa and Merrick histories overlap across the south shore.
why_this_matters: Massapeoque Meadows presents wetlands as Indigenous homelands and working landscapes. Salt meadows supported hunting, fishing, shellfishing, travel, and later colonial claims over land and resources.
